'''Ian Mahinmi''' (born November 5, 1986) is a French former professional [[basketball]] player. He played the [[Center (basketball)|center]] position and was selected with the 28th overall pick in the [[2005 NBA draft]] by the [[San Antonio Spurs]].

==Early life==
Mahinmi was born to a [[Benin]]ese<ref name=nbaprofile>[http://www.nba.com/playerfile/ian_mahinmi/bio.html Ian Mahinmi biography] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120211053140/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/ian_mahinmi/bio.html |date=2012-02-11 }}. NBA.com</ref> father who helped other Africans immigrate to France and a [[Jamaica]]n<ref name=nbaprofile/> mother who taught in a preschool. Mahinmi preferred playing soccer as a child along with his older brother, but eventually switched to playing basketball. He was 6 feet tall when he was 14 years old.

==Professional career==

=== Le Havre (2003–2006) ===
[[File:Ian Mahinmi 1 cropped.jpg|thumb|left|upright|Mahinmi in 2007]]
Mahinmi made his impression on international scouts at the 2004 Under-18 European Championships in Zaragoza, Spain. It was there that he first caught the attention of international scouts, including [[San Antonio Spurs]] scout [[Sam Presti]]. After playing with the French national team he signed his first contract with the club [[Saint Thomas Basket Le Havre|STB Le Havre]] (France). He played three seasons with Le Havre, averaging 9.7 points and 5.2 rebounds per game in 2005–06.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ian Mahinmi - Basket Info |url=http://www.basketinfo.com/joueur.php?no_joueur=1349 |access-date=2023-12-07 |website=www.basketinfo.com}}</ref>

=== Pau-Orthez (2006–2007) ===
In the summer of 2006, Mahinmi signed a contract to play for [[Élan Béarnais Pau-Orthez|Pau Orthez]] in France's top professional league.  He averaged 4.3 points and 3.2 rebounds in 12.7 minutes in the 2006–07 season, helping the team win the French Cup.

===San Antonio Spurs (2007–2010)===
Mahinmi was selected 28th overall in the [[2005 NBA draft]] by the [[San Antonio Spurs]], which surprised many other teams and league officials because he wasn't among the 128 players listed in the league's draft guide. Mahinmi was considered a "project" that would be a couple of years from competing in the NBA. The Spurs' interest in Mahinmi related to their need for an athletic big man since [[David Robinson (basketball)|David Robinson]] retired. Playing for the Spurs' 2006 summer-league team at [[Rocky Mountain Revue]], Mahinmi demonstrated his athleticism, but had difficulty maintaining rebounding or post position without fouling. After Mahinmi moved to Pau Orthez, which had a more developed strength and nutrition program than the one at Le Havre, the Spurs also began to send a strength coach to monitor his progress.<ref>[http://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/basketball/nba/spurs/stories/MYSA073006.01C.BKNspurs.mahinmi.1759f2a.html Spurs' 2005 draft pick Mahinmi remains intriguing work in progress] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070929105939/http://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/basketball/nba/spurs/stories/MYSA073006.01C.BKNspurs.mahinmi.1759f2a.html |date=2007-09-29 }}, MySA.com, July 29, 2006</ref>

During the 2007 Summer League, Mahinmi tore his right [[pectoralis minor]] shortly after the start of play. Despite this setback, he was signed by the Spurs on August 23, 2007.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/mahinmi_070823.html Spurs Sign Ian Mahinmi]</ref> On October 30, 2007, Mahinmi made his NBA debut with the Spurs against the [[Portland Trail Blazers]], playing only 74 seconds and registering no statistics.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20071102080502/http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=271030024 Spurs' quest to repeat kicks off with win over Blazers]</ref> Mahinmi played for the [[Austin Toros]], the Spurs' affiliate in the [[NBA Development League]], by November.<ref>[http://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/basketball/nba/spurs/stories/MYSA101707.01C.Spurs.en.33f6670.html Spurs: Rookies could be Toros teammates] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071019013106/http://www.mysanantonio.com/sports/basketball/nba/spurs/stories/MYSA101707.01C.Spurs.en.33f6670.html |date=2007-10-19 }}, MySA.com, October 16, 2007</ref> Mahinmi averaged 17.1 points and 8.2 rebounds in the NBA Development League, leading the Austin Toros to the D-League Finals in which they lost.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/dleague/playerfile/index.jsp?player=ian_mahinmi NBA Development League: Ian Mahinmi Playerfile] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080624043149/http://www.nba.com/dleague/playerfile/index.jsp?player=ian_mahinmi |date=2008-06-24 }}</ref>

===Dallas Mavericks (2010–2012)===
Mahinmi signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]] on July 13, 2010.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=6214 |title=Mavericks sign Ian Mahinmi |access-date=2012-05-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100715110057/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=6214 |archive-date=2010-07-15 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On December 7, 2010, against the [[Golden State Warriors]], Mahinmi recorded his first career [[double-double]] (12 points and 10 rebounds in 21 minutes).<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20101207/GSWDAL/gameinfo.html |title=Warriors-Mavericks notebook |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2012-05-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110321162835/http://www.nba.com/games/20101207/GSWDAL/gameinfo.html |archive-date=2011-03-21 |url-status=dead }}</ref> On January 15, 2011, Mahinmi scored a career high 17 points in a loss to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]], going 6–6 from the floor and 5–6 from the free throw line while collecting 6 rebounds. On March 20, 2011, Mahinmi collected a career-high 13 rebounds and 9 points after playing 20 minutes in the 101–73 win over the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=310320006|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110324152548/http://espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=310320006|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 24, 2011|title=Dirk Nowitzki, Peja Stojakovic help Mavs to 11th straight playoff berth|date=2011-03-21|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2016-07-08}}</ref>

On June 12, 2011, in game 6 of the NBA Finals against the [[Miami Heat]] with Dallas leading the series 3–2, Mahinmi collected a crucial offensive rebound in the closing seconds of the 3rd quarter before hitting a buzzer beater shot to further extend the Mavericks lead. Dallas went on to win the game 105–95 and Mahinmi won his first [[NBA Finals|NBA championship]] with the [[Dallas Mavericks]].

During the [[2011 NBA lockout]], Mahinmi played four games for [[STB Le Havre]]. In December 2011, he returned to the Mavericks. He scored a career high 19 points on December 30, 2011, in a game against the [[Toronto Raptors]] as the Mavericks won their first game of the [[2011–12 Dallas Mavericks season|2011–12 season]]. Mahinmi went 6–6 from the floor and 7–11 from the free throw line while collecting 5 rebounds.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20111230/TORDAL/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Mavericks 99, Raptors 86|last=Ivey|first=Dave|date=2011-12-30|website=NBA.com|access-date=2016-07-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120107190053/http://www.nba.com/games/20111230/TORDAL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=2012-01-07|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Mahinmi recorded his first career start in a 95–86 loss to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20120201/OKCDAL/gameinfo.html|title=Notebook: Thunder 95, Mavs 86|last=Ivey|first=Dave|date=2012-02-01|website=NBA.com|access-date=2016-07-08|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120209220200/http://www.nba.com/games/20120201/OKCDAL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=2012-02-09|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Indiana Pacers (2012–2016)===
On July 12, 2012, Mahinmi was traded to the [[Indiana Pacers]] in exchange for [[Darren Collison]] and [[Dahntay Jones]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/pacers/news/its-official-pacers-acquire-mahinmi-trade-collison-jones|title=It's Official: Pacers Acquire Mahinmi for Collison, Jones|date=2012-07-12|website=Indiana Pacers|access-date=2016-07-08}}</ref>

In his 2014–15 year with the Indiana Pacers, Ian recorded the lowest free throw percentage in the history of the NBA, with a percentage of 30.49%. As a result, Mahinmi almost never played in the fourth quarter as teams would intentionally foul him to get extra possessions and limiting the Pacers' [[Offensive rating]].

On February 19, 2016, Mahinmi matched a career high with 19 points and grabbed 11 rebounds in a 101–98 win over the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{Cite On March 4, 2016, Mahinmi led the Pacers with a career-high 14 rebounds and 10 points in 32 minutes in a 101–108 loss to the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{Cite 25 points, Pacers beat Rockets 104–101|date=2016-03-27|website=ESPN.com|access-date=2016-07-08}}</ref> In Game 4 of the Pacers' 2016 first-round playoff series against the [[Toronto Raptors]], Mahinmi April 12, 2017, he was ruled out for the start of the postseason with a strained left calf.<ref>{{cite On July 6, 2021, Mahinmi announced his retirement from professional basketball.<ref>{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Ian Mahinmi Announces Retirement|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2021/07/ian-mahinmi-announces-retirement.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|access-date=July 6, 2021|date=July 6, 2021}}</ref>
